string.text: Thank you for using Party AI Controls! To access the configuration panel, press {KEYBIND}!
Choose which parties to directly command
Parties must be manageable and in visual range to appear here.
Manage garrison parties for your clan.
If you are the ruler of your kingdom, manage garrisons for the entire kingdom instead of just your clan.
Cannot manage garrison parties without allowing troop conversion.
Allows troop conversion for lord parties. This setting is no longer required to manage lord party troop composition. Use the recruitment order to make sure your parties recruit the troops you want.
Allows troop conversion for caravans. At present this setting is necessary to manage caravan troop composition.
Allows troop conversion for garrisons. At present this setting is necessary to manage garrison troop composition.

Manage caravans for your clan. Caravan settings are saved separately from regular party settings, so you can have heroes with both. In order to manage their troops properly, the mod needs to have troop conversion enabled for caravans.
If you are the ruler of your kingdom, manage parties for the entire kingdom instead of just your clan.

If enabled, all AI patrols will attack any parties that come in range if they can catch them. Amends the 'Patrolling around X' AI behavior to include searching for targets--normally they wander aimlessly and don't attack anything. This is applied across the board, so you may not want to enable it until you're in the vassal/kingdom stage so there'll be more bandits.
AI will fallback to patrolling its clan territory when there is nothing else to do. Applies to any lord party not managed by the mod.
Automatically create clan parties for heroes that are available. Parties will not be created for heroes that are in your party.
Keybind to open this control panel. If you lock yourself out with a broken key combo, use partyai.open in the console to get back here and fix it.
Keybind to choose which parties to directly command. Press ALT+X (default) to choose nearby parties, then hold ALT (default) to order them around.
Keybind to command nearby parties. Press ALT+X (default) to choose nearby parties, then hold ALT (default) to order them around.
Heroes that we are allowed to create parties for. If blank, all available heroes will be considered.
Limits the maximum amount of clan parties that will be auto created.
Allow troops to be automatically converted to the ones in your assigned party template. Cost is adjusted if needed.

Enable or disable management of specific types of parties. You can change these at any time. If you disable a category that was previously managed, your settings for those parties will be ignored until you enable management again.

Amount of troops to convert to a party template per day. This value is per-party and applies to all managed parties, caravans, and garrisons. Helps protect against large spikes in cost from changing templates, and just makes it feel a little less awkward than magically converting 300 troops at once.
Select which heroes to automatically create parties for
PartyAIControls: You've changed your control panel keybind. If you've accidentally locked yourself out, run partyai.open in the console to get back into the control panel.
Show all heroes that can lead parties. Useful for assigning settings for any potential hero that might be a leader.
Copy settings from one party to another. Select the checkbox next to a party and press CTRL-C or this button.
Paste settings from one party to another. After copying, select the checkboxes next to all parties you want to paste to and press CTRL-V or this button.
Select which troops along the upgrade paths you've chosen to be included in the party template. The topmost troop in the list will be the portrait next to the template.
Must select at least one troop that upgrades to {CHARACTER}
The caravan will only visit settlements in this list.
Maximum troop tier to upgrade troops to. If you lower this setting while there are higher tier troops in the party, they will be downgraded.
Allow this party to join kingdom armies. Even with this setting disabled the party will be allowed to join your army.
Allow this party to donate troops to friendly garrisons.
Allow this party to besiege towns and castles. If disabled, parties will leave armies that are sieging, refunding the influence to the army leader.
Allow this party to raid hostile villages. If disabled, parties will leave armies that are raiding, refunding the influence to the army leader.
Allow this party to take enemy lords prisoner after battle. If disabled, parties will release captured lords.
Allow this party to recruit troops. If you disable this setting, you will have to supply the party with troops manually. If you do not, you can expect the AI to behave stupidly.

Buy enough horses to mount your troops on foot in order to increase movement speed. If you set the budget to zero, this will still prevent unncessary selling of horses. Please note that some horse types do not count towards the speed bonus, like Sumpter Horses in native. This feature won't treat a horse as providing a speed bonus unless the game treats it that way in native or whatever overhaul you play.

Automatically set an order to go recruiting when party is below X% of it's max party size. The order will only be added if there is not an existing order to recruit troops in the queue and you are not directly commanding the party.
Order to issue when the party is not in an army and has no current order.
Party will go on a recruitment run when under this percentage of its maximum troops.
These values are not useful for caravans unless you enable troop conversion in the mod options.
Templates are not useful for caravans unless you enable troop conversion in the mod options.
This hero is an army leader. Orders given to their party will apply to their entire army.
Select which template to fine tune
Select a new template for {LEADER}'s Party
Select a new template for {SETTLEMENT}'s Garrison
Choose which type of order to add

Order the party leader to only focus on recruiting troops. If they have an assigned troop template, they will only visit settlements that offer those troops. Keep in mind these settlements may be far away.

Patrol an area around the target settlement. The party will visit villages and towns to restock its troops and supplies. Bandits and other enemies will be chased down if the party leader believes they can be caught. The party will defend villages and castles/towns within its patrol radius from raids and sieges.
Visit a settlement but don't stay there.
Stay in the settlement. Will not defend the settlement if it is under siege and the party is outside the walls.
The party or army will besiege the target settlement. The order will be cleared upon capturing the city or by the attacking army being defeated.
Stay in the garrison of the settlement. The party may make occassional visits to other settlements for food if there is not enough food in the settlement to buy.
Select which settings you would like to copy.
You may select more than one option.
Select which parties to copy settings to
Are you sure you want to delete the template {TEMPLATE}?
Enter a name for your new party troop template.
There is already a template with that name.
{NAME} is out of range to be commanded directly
PartyAIControls: Feature to enable armies without being a Vassal is not compatible with BannerKings.
{HERO} has created a new party near {SETTLEMENT}
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because they were called to {ARMY}
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because their food supplies ran low.
Let me inspect your party's inventory.
Percentage must be greater than zero
Automatically hand all player formations to the native tactical AI after deployment. Your character remains under your control, and the battle commander key toggles command at any time.
Toggle between native AI command and your previous formation control state during battle.
The battle AI now commands your formations. You still control your character. Press {KEYBIND} to resume command.
You have resumed command of your formations.
Battle AI command is unavailable in this mission.
This formation class is not used by this party's template.
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because their target is invalid.
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because no suitable target could be found.
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because the target's faction is no longer an enemy.
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because the target is under siege.
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because their target is not reachable.
{PARTY} is no longer {ORDER} because the target's faction became an enemy.
You must load a save game to use this menu.
It doesn't make sense to dismiss troops when troop conversion is enabled--they can be converted into whatever troop you want.
Change radius for patrol orders. Adjust it until it produces the result you want. The percentage is relative to the default radius.
Allow this party to take troops from your garrisons.
Dismiss troops that do not fit the party template or the chosen composition percentages. This only happens above the specified party-size percentage so the party does not leave itself vulnerable.
The party starts dismissing troops that do not fit its template once it exceeds this percentage of its maximum size.
Allow this party to recruit troops from enemy settlements. This can help parties operating behind enemy lines, but is risky.
Adds a power-aware combined-arms tactic that competes normally with native tactics instead of overriding them. Realistic Battle AI still takes priority.
You cannot resume formation command while your character is incapacitated.
AI troops near the predicted impact point of heavy siege projectiles briefly scatter, then return to native siege behavior. Troops in melee or using siege objects are not interrupted.
Battle estimate: {ALLY} vs {ENEMY} troops; allied combat power is about {POWER}% of the enemy.
Headcounts are close, but troop tiers, equipment and unit matchups put your side at a real disadvantage.

While the main party is in a safe town, automatically pay for at most one caravan per day until the configured limit is reached. The best available companion is selected by trade, scouting and tactics skill.
Create the more expensive caravan variant with stronger starting guards.
Maximum number of active player-clan caravans. Max removes the limit.
A caravan is only formed if this much gold remains after paying its creation cost.
{HERO} formed an automatically managed caravan in {SETTLEMENT} for {COST}{GOLD_ICON}.
Choose what happens after this party enters a town or village. Full Auto also balances its template and equips party heroes from inventory.
Party AI: recruited {RECRUITED}, upgraded {UPGRADED}, balanced {BALANCED}, equipped {EQUIPPED}.
Import a validated troop template and composition from an HTTPS JSON URL.
Paste the HTTPS URL of a Party AI template JSON file.
A template download is already running.
Allow Party AI to manage player-clan towns and castles using the settings below.
Enable Town AI for This Fief
Allow Town AI to manage this settlement while global town management is enabled.
Strategy used by new fiefs and existing fiefs that follow global defaults. Economy prioritizes prosperity and revenue from taxes, tariffs, workshops and villages.

Balanced covers food, security, prosperity and defense; Stability protects loyalty, security and food; Economy prioritizes prosperity and revenue from taxes, tariffs, workshops and villages; Military prioritizes walls, militia and garrisons. Loyalty and food emergencies override the selected focus.
Choose and reorder construction projects according to the selected strategy and current emergencies.
Select a continuous project when no building should be constructed or an emergency needs attention.
Move player gold into a settlement's construction reserve without spending below the configured player reserve.
Move player gold into this settlement's construction reserve within the global player-gold limit.
Automatic construction funding never reduces player gold below this amount.
Stop adding construction funds after the settlement reserve reaches this amount.
Stop adding construction funds after this settlement's reserve reaches this amount.
Maximum construction funds that Town AI may add to one settlement per day.
Below this loyalty value, stability projects take precedence over the selected strategy.
Treat a projected food shortage within this many days as an emergency.
Recommend suitable governors or assign them automatically. Automatic assignment only uses eligible player-clan heroes.
Allow automatic governor mode to replace an existing governor when a meaningfully better candidate is available.
Minimum days before Town AI may replace a governor it assigned.
Temporarily redirect suitable player-clan parties to threatened settlements and restore their previous orders afterwards.
Allow Town AI to assign suitable player-clan parties when this settlement is threatened.
Use automatic defense for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Higher-priority settlements receive available defenders before lower-priority settlements with similar threats.
Defense priority used by new fiefs and existing fiefs that follow global defaults.
Map radius used to count hostile parties near a settlement.
Dispatch defenders when nearby hostile strength reaches this share of local defense strength.
Restore defenders' previous orders after threat falls below this ratio. Keep it lower than the dispatch ratio.
Only dispatch parties at or above this share of their party-size limit.
Number of eligible clan parties Town AI must leave unassigned as a mobile reserve.
Maximum clan parties Town AI may assign to one settlement at the same time.
Keep a defender assigned for at least this many days unless its order becomes invalid.
Wait this many days after release before automatically assigning the same party again.
Desired combined defense strength for fiefs following global defaults. Zero calculates a target from fief type, prosperity and priority.
Desired combined local defense strength. Zero lets Town AI calculate a target.
Allow assigned defenders whose party options permit donations to transfer troops once on arrival while preserving their minimum force.
Stop automatic troop donations after the garrison reaches this many troops. Zero uses each settlement's target.
Maximum share of an assigned party's troops that may be donated during one assignment.
Never reduce an assigned party below this troop count when donating to a garrison.
Desired garrison troop count for automatic reinforcement. Zero disables the fixed target.
Only garrison troops are managed here because this fief does not belong to the player clan.
{HERO} has been assigned as governor of {SETTLEMENT}.
Apply Defaults to Existing Fiefs on Save
Make all current player-clan towns and castles follow these defaults. Each fief's enabled/disabled state is preserved.
Keep this fief synchronized with global construction, governor and defense defaults. The fief enable switch remains independent.
Global enable is the master switch. A fief may either follow the global defaults or keep explicit local settings.
Automatic mode assigns an eligible unassigned player-clan hero on the next daily town update. Recommend mode only reports the best candidate.

Food or loyalty emergencies temporarily outrank profit. Economy strategy otherwise favors taxes, tariffs, prosperity, workshops, villages and lower garrison costs. Listed net income is an operational estimate, not the clan finance total.
Paused: global town management is off.
No governor; Town AI is paused.
No governor; governor management is off.
No governor; no eligible unassigned clan hero is available.
No governor; recommended: {HERO}. Switch to Assign to appoint automatically.
No governor; {HERO} will be assigned when these settings are saved or on the next daily update.
Food emergency: {FOOD} stock, {CHANGE}/day; estimated days remaining: {DAYS}. Stabilization has priority.
Loyalty emergency: {LOYALTY}. Stability has priority over profit.
Prosperity {PROSPERITY}; food change {FOOD}; tariffs {TARIFFS}, projects {PROJECTS}, villages {VILLAGES}, garrison wage {WAGE}; listed net {NET}.
Enable building-queue management for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Enable daily-project management for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Enable automatic construction funding for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Allow governor replacement for fiefs that follow global defaults. Empty governor slots use unassigned heroes first.
Governor mode used by new fiefs and existing fiefs that follow global defaults. Assign appoints eligible unassigned clan heroes automatically.
Construction reserve target for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Daily construction funding limit for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Loyalty emergency threshold for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Food-emergency horizon for fiefs that follow global defaults.
Governor reassignment cooldown for fiefs that follow global defaults. Empty governor slots ignore reassignment cooldown.
Target garrison troop count for fiefs following global defaults. Zero disables the fixed target.
Create a clan party, enable caravan management, or acquire a fief to manage it here.
Select one row to copy its settings.
One source selected. Copy to continue.
Copied from {SOURCE}. Select one or more compatible targets.
